title: Applied Population Dynamics
text: Foundations of population dynamics from an applied perspective. Exponential and logistic population growth, life tables, species interactions, and stochastic models for structured populations. Sampling design and analytical methods for estimating abundance and demographic parameters. Application of population models to harvest management and conversation of small populations. Integrative student project required.

title: Applied Population Dynamics
text:
Course Objectives and Learning Outcomes
This course will present the theory necessary for understanding wildlife population dynamics, and it will explain how to use theory and data to inform management and conservation efforts. By the end of the course, students will be able to: (1) Develop models to forecast the impacts of environmental change and management actions on wildlife populations; (2) Design field studies to collect data on wildlife demographics; (3) Use statistical software to analyze data on wildlife populations; (4) Review scientific literature to support modeling decisions; (5) Present modeling results in a short scientific paper and an oral presentation.

title: Applied Population Dynamics
text:
Learning objectives
By the end of the semester, you should be able to:

Develop a population model that:

Describes variation in demographic parameters over time
Predicts how a population will respond to management and conservation actions.

Design a study to collect the data necessary to estimate the demographic parameters of the model.
Use R software to estimate parameters from field data.
